timeline.title: A Short History of Celebrating Mum
items: Mothering Sunday
In England, young people working away were given a day off to go home to their mothers, often with flowers picked on the way.
A call for peace
Julia Ward Howe wrote a Mother's Day Proclamation, asking mothers everywhere to unite for peace.
A daughter remembers
Anna Jarvis held a service for her own mother and handed out carnations, her mother's favourite flower.
A day for every mum
Mother's Day became a national holiday in the United States, and the idea spread around the world.
today: Not in the history books yet. But to us, the most important mum who ever lived.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Mums
items: Mother is the name for God in the lips and hearts of little children.
William Makepeace Thackeray, Vanity Fair, 1848
A mother is the truest friend we have.
Washington Irving, 1820
All that I am, or hope to be, I owe to my angel mother.
Abraham Lincoln
An ounce of mother is worth a pound of clergy.
An old Spanish saying
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: thank you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of a Mother's Love
items: heart
Before hello
Babies can recognise their mother's voice before they are even born.
eye
Her face first
Newborns can pick out their mother's face from others within days of birth.
pulse
The calming voice
Just hearing mum's voice can lower a child's stress and release oxytocin, the cuddle hormone.
spark
Part of her forever
A few of a child's cells can stay in their mother's body for decades. Scientists call it microchimerism.
smile
The first smile
Babies begin smiling back at the people who love them at around six weeks old.
moon
The night shift
In a baby's first year, mums give up hundreds of hours of sleep. Most would do it all again.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It still cannot explain how {who} always knows.

note.title: Why we made this for her
paras: Every family has a woman at its centre. She remembers every birthday, sets every table and somehow always knows what to say.
She is rarely thanked properly, because she is too busy looking after everyone else.
{who}, this magazine is everyone you have ever looked after, saying thank you at last.
From everything {from} told us, you are the heart of this family.

own.dayTitle: A Day in the Life of {first}
day: The kettle is on before the house is awake.
Rings round the whole family. Knows everything by ten.
Cooks for twelve. Sits down last, as always.
Someone always pops in. Someone always leaves with leftovers.
night: Says a little prayer for every one of us by name.
guide: The head of the table, where she belongs
Whatever is left once everyone else has eaten
Holding everyone together without anyone noticing
Whenever the family needs her, which is always
Let her sit down. Ask her stories. Thank her every chance you get
little: You remember every birthday, anniversary and exam result.
You make the whole family feel like one big home.
You never let anyone leave hungry, or without a hug.
You carry the family's worries so we do not have to.
